name: Category Flexibility
definition: The ability to generate or use different sets of rules for combining or grouping things in different ways.

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: Icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind): brute-force search over a hand-written library of 142 grid functions (a domain-specific language)
benchmark.metric: percent of tasks solved (top-3 accuracy) on the 100-task hidden private test set
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce (typical adults doing novel visual rule-induction puzzles)

benchmark.name: Bongard-LOGO
benchmark.metric: test accuracy (%) on the free-form shape (FF) test split; chance = 50
benchmark.human_reference: General educated adults doing few-shot visual concept induction. These are non-expert solvers, comparable to the 'Human (Amateur)' baseline in Nie et al.

benchmark.name: ARC
benchmark.model_or_system: icecuber (winner of the 2020 ARC competition on Kaggle, a program-synthesis/DSL search solver)
benchmark.metric: percent of hidden private-test tasks solved (exact-match output, up to 3 attempts per task in the 2020 Kaggle protocol)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population, typical educated workers doing novel rule-induction and regrouping tasks without specialist training

benchmark.name: OCW
benchmark.metric: percent of test walls fully solved (all 4 groups correct)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population doing lateral-thinking grouping puzzles, calibrated against Only Connect contestants (a strong, self-selected quiz population)

benchmark.name: NYT Connections
benchmark.metric: leaderboard score on a 0-100 scale (mean per-puzzle score on NYT Connections puzzles)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult English speakers who do word and category puzzles, i.e. typical NYT Connections players rather than expert puzzlers.

benchmark.name: Extended NYT Connections
benchmark.metric: Percent score (mean share of correct groups per puzzle, with the linear partial credit used in 2025)
benchmark.human_reference: General educated adults who do word and category puzzles (typical NYT Connections players), used as a proxy for people applying category flexibility in work settings

benchmark.name: NYT Connections Extended
benchmark.metric: Leaderboard score in percent, using quadratic-v1 scoring: the mean over puzzles of (exact groups found / 4)^2, times 100
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population, specifically adults who regularly do word and category puzzles such as NYT Connections players. Category flexibility is a general cognitive ability, not a specialist skill.
